sections.heading: Traps catch rats. Sealing stops them.
sections.body:
Roof rats travel along citrus trees, block walls and power lines, and a young one can fit through a gap the size of a quarter. Traps alone mean a new tenant every few weeks.

We inspect the whole envelope, from roof line to slab, and close every gap with steel mesh, flashing and sealant that rodents cannot chew. Then we trap out the ones already inside, check back until the activity stops, and clean up the attic they left behind.

items.question: Roof rats or mice: how can I tell?
items.answer: Roof rat droppings are about half an inch long with pointed ends; mouse droppings are smaller, like grains of rice. Noise in the attic at night usually means roof rats.

items.question: Do you use poison?
items.answer: Rarely, and never inside the home. Poisoned rodents can die in a wall void and smell for weeks. We rely on exclusion and snap traps, with tamper-proof bait stations outside where appropriate.

items.question: How long does exclusion take?
items.answer: Most homes are sealed in a single day. We then return for trap checks over the following two weeks.

items.question: Is the work guaranteed?
items.answer: Yes. Exclusion work carries a one-year guarantee. If a rodent gets in through a sealed point, we come back and fix it free.

items.question: Can you clean up the attic?
items.answer: Yes. We remove droppings and nesting, sanitise the area and replace damaged insulation where needed.
